key_insight: Sb doping in Cs2BInCl6 double perovskite nanocrystals creates bright, composition-tunable self-trapped exciton emission, while Na-to-K alloying mainly shifts the lattice distortion and therefore the photoluminescence color and polarization anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: This points to a practical way to tune lead-free perovskite optoelectronic emission using composition control, with polarization-resolved signatures that can help diagnose exciton localization and materials quality.
method: Optical spectroscopy of Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals with B-site alloying from Na to K
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states, dopant-hybridized in-gap levels, and lattice distortions
Time-resolved polarization-anisotropy measurements to test predicted STE wavefunction structure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a photoluminescence shift from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV across compositions, nearly unchanged absorption near 3.8 eV, and close agreement between predicted and measured anisotropy.
watch_item: Because the key effects rely on strong exciton-phonon coupling and self-trapping, the same composition tuning may not translate directly to high-efficiency charge extraction or device architectures.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
